questions.question: A hiker in Connecticut finds a deer tick attached to his leg. A week later he develops a bull's-eye rash and swollen knees, and testing shows a bacterial infection carried by the tick. By what method was this organism spread?
questions.explanation: The tick is an animal that carried the organism to the patient, which is exactly how vector-borne spread works.

questions.question: After a summer of heavy rain, mosquitoes multiply around a Florida neighborhood. Several residents with no travel history develop dengue fever, and trapped mosquitoes test positive for the virus. What type of transmission is responsible?
questions.explanation: The mosquitoes are the living carriers moving the virus from person to person, so the spread is vector-borne.

questions.question: Your crew responds to a home where the family's free-roaming dogs sleep indoors covered in ticks. A child in the home has a high fever and a spotted rash and is diagnosed with Rocky Mountain spotted fever. The organism reached the child through which route?
questions.explanation: The ticks on the dogs are the animal vectors that delivered the bacteria to the child.

questions.question: An EMT student is asked to classify a patient's illness: a virus has invaded the patient's body, is multiplying, and is producing fever and a cough. What general term describes a medical condition caused this way?
questions.explanation: The condition is produced by harmful organisms growing and spreading inside the body, which is the definition of an infectious disease.

questions.question: Your crew transports three residents from the same nursing home in one shift, all with vomiting and diarrhea traced to a norovirus multiplying in their digestive tracts. Each resident's condition is an example of what?
questions.explanation: A harmful organism spreading within each patient's body caused the illness, making each case an infectious disease.

questions.question: A diabetic patient has a foot wound, but the redness, swelling, and fever come from bacteria invading and multiplying in the tissue rather than from the injury itself. What type of medical condition has developed in the wound?
questions.explanation: Bacteria growing and spreading within the body's tissues created a new condition, which is an infectious disease.

questions.question: A paramedic with 12 years on the job has felt drained for months. She has become cynical about patients, dreads every shift, and her assessments are not as sharp as they used to be after years of mandatory overtime. What has she developed?
questions.explanation: Exhaustion plus cynicism plus reduced performance building up from long-term job stress is the classic picture of burnout.

questions.question: An EMT who once volunteered for every community event now feels emotionally numb, snaps at frequent-flyer patients, and is making documentation errors after two years of short staffing and back-to-back shifts. His supervisor should recognize which condition?
questions.explanation: His detachment and cynicism, exhaustion, and declining work quality all grew out of chronic job stress, matching burnout rather than a single bad call.

questions.question: After years of night shifts and rising call volume, a medic tells his partner, 'I just don't care anymore, and I'm not the clinician I was.' He is tired all the time and his performance reviews have slipped. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.explanation: Long-term job stress has produced the three defining features: exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance.

questions.question: Which term is defined as: The use of an animal to spread an organism from one person or place to another.
questions.explanation: vector-borne transmission: The use of an animal to spread an organism from one person or place to another.

questions.question: What does the term "vector-borne transmission" mean?
choices: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) is caused by HIV, which damages the cells in the body's immune system so that the body is unable to fight infection or certain cancers.
The individual in the department who is charged with the responsibility of managing exposures and infection control.
The use of an animal to spread an organism from one person or place to another.
questions.explanation: vector-borne transmission: The use of an animal to spread an organism from one person or place to another.

questions.question: In August 1999, an outbreak of encephalitis struck Queens, New York City, at the same time as a large die-off of crows and exotic birds at the Bronx Zoo. Investigators identified West Nile virus, never before recorded in the Western Hemisphere; 62 human cases were confirmed and 7 people died. The virus was carried from infected birds to humans by Culex pipiens mosquitoes. What should EMS crews take from this case?
choices: Crews should assume encephalitis clusters are spread person to person and wear respirators on every outdoor call.
Crews should focus on the sick birds as the direct source and handle dead birds without gloves to speed up the scene.
Crews should avoid outdoor scenes entirely during mosquito season until public health clears the area.
Crews should treat clusters of encephalitis in mosquito season as a possible arbovirus event and use repellent and skin coverage on outdoor scenes.
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes acting as vectors carried West Nile virus from birds to people, so repellent and skin coverage protect crews during mosquito season.

questions.question: In late 1975, mothers in Lyme, Connecticut reported an unusual cluster of children with swollen joints diagnosed as juvenile arthritis. Yale researchers linked the illness to bites from deer ticks, and in 1982 the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi was identified inside the ticks. What should this case prompt an EMT to do when assessing outdoor and rural patients?
choices: Ask outdoor and rural patients about recent air travel and check their temperature before anything else.
Assume joint swelling in children is always a sports injury and skip questions about insect exposure.
Check only the patient's scalp for ticks, since ticks never attach anywhere else on the body.
Ask outdoor and rural patients about tick exposure and check for attached ticks and the bull's-eye rash during assessment.
questions.explanation: Lyme disease is spread by tick bites, so asking about tick exposure and checking for ticks and the bull's-eye rash catches it early.

questions.question: Which term is defined as: A medical condition caused by the growth and spread of small, harmful organisms within the body.
questions.explanation: infectious disease: A medical condition caused by the growth and spread of small, harmful organisms within the body.

questions.question: What does the term "infectious disease" mean?
choices: Inflammation of the liver, usually caused by a viral infection, that causes fever, loss of appetite, nausea, intestinal upset, and often jaundice.
The body's ability to protect itself from acquiring a disease.
A medical condition caused by the growth and spread of small, harmful organisms within the body.
Exposure or transmission of a communicable disease from one person to another by physical contact.
questions.explanation: infectious disease: A medical condition caused by the growth and spread of small, harmful organisms within the body.

questions.question: In July 1976, attendees of the American Legion convention at a Philadelphia hotel developed a severe, mysterious pneumonia; 182 people became ill and 29 died. Investigators eventually found a previously unknown bacterium, Legionella pneumophila, breeding in the hotel's air-conditioning cooling tower and spreading through the building in water droplets. What is the key lesson for an EMT who notices several patients with severe pneumonia tied to the same building?
choices: The crew should enter the building's mechanical areas to inspect the cooling tower themselves before reporting anything.
Clusters of severe pneumonia linked to one building or water system should be reported early, because the pattern is the clue to the organism.
Each pneumonia patient should be treated as an isolated case, since patients from the same building rarely share a cause.
Patients should be told the illness is most likely a common cold virus and does not need follow-up.
questions.explanation: The Legionnaires' outbreak was solved by recognizing the pattern of cases linked to one building, so early reporting of clusters is the clue to the organism.

questions.question: On September 28, 2014, a Dallas Fire-Rescue crew transported Thomas Eric Duncan, who became the first Ebola case diagnosed in the United States. The three crew members were placed in home isolation for 21 days, and the ambulance stayed in service for about 48 hours before it was quarantined, exposing gaps in notification. What does this case teach about infection control before the patient is ever loaded?
choices: Infection control begins only after arrival at the hospital, when the receiving facility takes over screening.
Crews should refuse transport for any patient with a fever until a physician clears them by phone.
Travel history and dispatch screening are infection control: identify the risk before the patient is in your ambulance.
The ambulance should be returned to service immediately after any transport to keep the fleet available.
questions.explanation: The Dallas Ebola transport showed that travel history and dispatch screening identify the risk before the patient is in the ambulance.

questions.question: Which term is defined as: A combination of exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance resulting from long-term job stresses.
questions.explanation: burnout: A combination of exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance resulting from long-term job stresses.

questions.question: What does the term "burnout" mean?
choices: Reactions to stress that occur during a stressful situation.

Securing a crashed vehicle with cribbing, struts, or other supports so it cannot move, shift, or roll; it must be done to ensure the vehicle is stable before attempting to access a patient trapped inside.
A combination of exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance resulting from long-term job stresses.
What PPE must be worn when blood or body fluids may splash into the eyes, noting that prescription glasses do not provide adequate protection because they offer little or no side protection.
questions.explanation: burnout: A combination of exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance resulting from long-term job stresses.

questions.question: The SNIPS study surveyed 1,112 US EMS providers in 2021 and found that almost 90% screened positive for burnout, with about 41.5% reporting mental health concerns at some point in their EMS careers; EMTs and women screened positive at higher rates than paramedics and men. How should an EMT view these findings?
choices: Assume burnout only affects new providers, so experienced EMTs do not need to monitor themselves.
Treat a positive burnout screening as a personal weakness that should be hidden from supervisors and partners.
Screen yourself honestly for burnout signs; at these rates it is an occupational hazard to manage, not a personal failure.
Wait until symptoms disappear on their own, since burnout screening has no value for working crews.
questions.explanation: With nearly 90% of surveyed EMS providers screening positive, burnout is an occupational hazard to manage, not a personal failure.

questions.question: During the spring 2020 COVID-19 peak, FDNY EMS handled a record of more than 6,500 calls in a single day. Three FDNY EMS workers died by suicide within a three-month period, calls to the department's counseling hotline rose 36%, and the department more than doubled its EMS peer counselors from 20 to 45 as crews described exhaustion and dread. What does this case show EMTs about getting help?
choices: A busy service should cut peer counselor positions first, since high call volume leaves no time to use them.
Counseling resources are meant for patients' families, not for EMS providers themselves.
Use peer support and counseling resources early; this case shows what happens to a whole service when burnout goes unaddressed.
Peer support should be used only after a provider has already decided to leave the profession.
questions.explanation: FDNY's experience shows burnout can overwhelm an entire service, so peer support and counseling should be used early, before it goes unaddressed.
